correctness.rationale: For every finite nonempty simple H with no even simple cycle, the symmetric difference of two distinct perfect matchings of an induced subgraph would contain an even alternating cycle; hence each such matching is unique. Every perfect matching of H□K2 therefore consists of paired horizontal lifts of an H-matching and rungs at its uncovered vertices. The face involution toggles the least uncovered rung unless projection covers H, then the upper lift at the least bottom-selected edge. Nonmatched directed arrows never add projection edges, so oriented Hasse cycles reduce to constant projection, where the pivot monotonicity rules them out. With H-perfect matching there is exactly one unmatched face of cardinality |V(H)|/2; otherwise none, including the empty face, proving S^{n/2-1} or a point via augmented discrete Morse. Independent exhaustive all 613 labeled no-even-cycle graphs of orders 1..5 confirmed exactly 92,400 augmented faces, 260,989 Hasse incidences and 585 cases with no critical face / 28 with one. The proof, not finite data, covers all graphs; the C4 even-cycle boundary is outside scope.
